proofs.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}
The assertion is conditional.  We therefore assume throughout this proof the
affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion named in the first clause
of the theorem; we do not assert that this conclusion follows from the standing
assumptions.  Written in the notation of the core, the part of that conditional
premise used below is the following.  There is a computable sequence
\(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) such that, for every
\(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\) and every \(j\), a finite record
\(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) is eventually produced and its
outward ledger certifies
\[
 \begin{split}
 c\{Q_j(K)\}&\ge 1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
 r\{Q_j(K)\}&\le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}&\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
 \end{split}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
Here \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of all semantic-label coverage probabilities
and \(r(Q)\) is the supremum of the separated diameter risk.  The premise also
certifies, by finite data, all canonical-section, positive-weight safety,
collar-discrepancy, translated-tail, and refinement-count obligations needed
to justify the three inequalities in (1).  Thus (1), rather than any unproved
amenability or trace assertion, is the precise conditional input to the
algorithm.

We now construct the procedure in \(\text{def:certglue-handle}\).  At integer
stage \(s\), enumerate all indices \(j\le s\), all records in
\(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) having code length at most \(s\), all exact
rational incidence forests and semantic projections belonging to those
records, and all rational integration and rounding precisions among the first
\(s\) choices.  For each such record \(Q\), the checks prescribed by
\(\text{def:weighted-error-ledger}\) return rational outward enclosures
\(c^-_{Q,s}\) and \(r^+_{Q,s}\) satisfying
\[
 c^-_{Q,s}\le c(Q),\qquad r(Q)\le r^+_{Q,s}.                    \tag{2}
\]
The record is accepted only after every polyhedral incidence, semantic
projection, protected-neighborhood, Gaussian-tail, covariance, quadrature,
and rounding entry needed for (2) has passed its finite rational check.
Consequently acceptance itself never uses an uncertified floating-point sign.

Intersect the coverage enclosure with \([0,1]\), and define
\[
 \rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},\qquad
 q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.                   \tag{3}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\) and \(0\le c^-_{Q,s}\le1\),
\[
 0\le\rho_{Q,s}\le1-\eta<1,
 \qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0.                                    \tag{4}
\]
Thus every division in (3) is valid.  Moreover (2)--(3) imply
\[
 c(Q)\ge c^-_{Q,s}\ge1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}.                       \tag{5}
\]
Apply \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) with
\(\rho=\rho_{Q,s}\).  The archived rule
\(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) is globally honest and
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 \le R_r(Q^+)
 \le r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.                                      \tag{6}
\]
All inputs in (3) have the exact finite encoding carried by
\(\mathfrak G\) and the record.  If the last expression in (6) is not itself
rational in that encoding, outward interval arithmetic supplies a rational
\(U_{Q,s}\) with
\[
 U_{Q,s}\ge r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.                               \tag{7}
\]
The interval is refined as \(s\) increases.  This preserves exact honesty;
only the reported upper endpoint is rounded outward.

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic dual records described in
\(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\): their weights are rational and
their support points have rational real-algebraic encodings.  Membership of a
support point in a finite union \(D_v\), and membership in \(H_r\), reduce to
finitely many exact polynomial-sign and convex quadratic-distance checks.
For each feasible dual \(\nu\), refine its Gaussian integrations until a
rational lower endpoint \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) for its objective is available.
Every such endpoint is a valid lower certificate by
\(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\).  Set
\[
 L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},\qquad
 U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s},                     \tag{8}
\]
leaving an endpoint undefined while the corresponding finite collection is
empty.  Weak duality and (6)--(7) give, whenever both endpoints are defined,
\[
 L_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_s.                        \tag{9}
\]

Every fixed stage terminates.  Indeed, its enumerated collections are finite;
rational polyhedral feasibility and incidence are finite rational linear
programs; and a requested Gaussian enclosure is obtained by integrating on a
rational box with interval subdivision and bounding the complement by the
recorded Gaussian tail.  On each compact box the integrands in an accepted
finite record have the certified moduli carried by that record, so subdivision
width tends to zero.  The Gaussian tail bound tends to zero as the box grows.
Hence a prescribed positive enclosure width is reached after finitely many
subdivisions.  These observations prove finite-stage termination and the
replayability of every accepted record.

It remains to prove that the outer gap eventually passes the stopping test.
By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is
\(K^*\in\mathcal C_\eta\) with
\[
 R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).                             \tag{10}
\]
Apply (1) to \(K^*\).  For any rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine
outward evaluation of the resulting finite record gives
\[
 c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\ge c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,qquad
 r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.                    \tag{11}
\]
Equations (1), (3), and (11) imply
\[
 \rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta.           \tag{12}
\]
Combining (1), (6), (10)--(12), and then allowing the outward interval in
(7) an additional width \(\zeta\), gives an accepted rational upper endpoint
satisfying
\[
 \begin{split}
 U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 &+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta\\
 &+\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
 {\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
 \end{split}                                                   \tag{13}
\]
The right side tends to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) by first increasing
\(j\) and then decreasing \(\zeta\), using \(\eta>0\).  On the lower side,
the last assertion of \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\) supplies an
increasing sequence of enumerated finite atomic certificates whose values
converge to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  Refinement of their outward lower
enclosures therefore yields
\[
 L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),\qquad
 \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).           \tag{14}
\]
Together with (9), (14) proves that some finite stage has
\(U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\).

Finally we expose the promised total recursive receipt.  For
\(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\), let
\(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of operations of type \(i\) executed
at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest bit length of an
integer occurring in that stage, including the input code.  These are
computable because the stage is finite.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C_i(0)&=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),&
 C_i(s+1)&=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),\\
 B(0)&=b(\mathfrak G,0),&
 B(s+1)&=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                  \tag{15}
\]
Let
\[
 s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=
 \min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\}.
                                                                    \tag{16}
\]
The test in (16) is a rational comparison, and (14) proves that its sequential
search halts for every encoded \((\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\).  Hence
\(s_*\) is total recursive.  The five advertised bounds are the explicit
total recursive functions
\[
 \begin{split}
 N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)&=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
 \quad i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\},\\
 \operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
 &=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
 \end{split}                                                       \tag{17}
\]
At stage \(s_*\), archive the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum
in (8) and the finite rational atomic dual attaining the finite maximum.
Equations (9), (16), and (17) give the claimed endpoints, gap, termination,
and cost receipt.  Every conclusion in this proof remains conditional on (1);
nothing here resolves the effective-compatible-density question.

\textbf{Technique: exact affine-slack coupling, finite-arrangement stability,
and parameter-independent Le Cam transfer.}
Fix a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\).  Let
\(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}=\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\),
and let \(A_\Psi\) have rows \(\alpha_j'\) for
\(j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}\), as in
\(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\).  Since every active cut satisfies
\(\psi_j(p_0)=0\),
\[
 c_n
 =A_\Psi\sqrt n\{p_n(0)-p_0\}.                                \tag{18}
\]
The local-family affine-hull assumption puts the vector after \(A_\Psi\)
in \(L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\); hence (18) and the definition of
\(\mathcal K_0\) give
\[
 c_n\in\mathcal K_0\qquad\text{for every }n.                  \tag{19}
\]
This proves compatibility of the observed moving offset rather than assuming
it.

Choose a positive rational \(\xi_n\downarrow0\).  The effective moving-offset
encoding assumption returns
\(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\cap\mathbb Q^{|\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}|}\)
with
\[
 \|\widehat c_n-c_n\|_\infty\le\xi_n.                         \tag{20}
\]
For every active facet, the exact identity in
\(\text{def:moving-slack-system}\) gives
\[
 \zeta_{n,j}(u)-(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u)
 =(c_{n,j}-\widehat c_{n,j})+e_{n,j}(u).                        \tag{21}
\]
Therefore, with
\(\delta_n(C)=\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\),
\[
 \max_j\sup_{u\in C}
 |\zeta_{n,j}(u)-(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u)|
 \le\delta_n(C)+\xi_n.                                        \tag{22}
\]
Because \(c_n\to c\) and (20) holds, all \(c_n\) and
\(\widehat c_n\), apart from finitely many, lie in one compact subset of
\(\mathcal K_0\).  Apply
\(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) on that compact offset
set.  It follows from (22), simultaneously for every completed semantic
union, that actual and \(\widehat c_n\)-offset label means on \(C\) can be
matched at Mahalanobis displacement at most
\[
 H_C\{\delta_n(C)+\xi_n\},                                     \tag{23}
\]
and that the corresponding distances to every rival semantic union change by
at most twice (23).  Equality faces cause no loss of a label because the
completed construction assigns every equality to all incident cells.  The
score-centering discrepancy is bounded by the centered expansion modulus
\(d_n(C)\).  Thus, after increasing the computable active-set constant if
necessary to absorb the factor two, every label and separated-risk matching
displacement is bounded by
\[
 H_C\chi_n(C),\qquad
 \chi_n(C)=d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)+\xi_n.                            \tag{24}
\]

We next charge possible sign changes without imposing a margin assumption.
For \(W_0\sim N_d(h,\Sigma_0)\),
\(c_j+a_j'W_0\) has variance
\(a_j'\Sigma_0a_j>0\): positivity follows from
\(a_j\ne0\) and \(\Sigma_0\succ0\).  Its density is bounded by
\(\{2\pi a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{-1/2}\), uniformly in \(c_j+a_j'h\).
Consequently, for every \(s\ge0\),
\[
 \Pr_h\{|c_j+a_j'W_0|\le s\}
 \le\min\left\{1,
 \frac{2s}{\sqrt{2\pi}\{a_j'\Sigma_0a_j\}^{1/2}}\right\}.     \tag{25}
\]
The union bound over the finite active list turns (25) exactly into
\(\mathfrak b_0(s)\).  If the actual and reference signs differ, (21)--(24)
show that either \(\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\), or the reference slack lies in the
band of width \(\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\).  Thus all moving-boundary failures have
probability at most
\[
 \mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}
 +\mathbf 1\{\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\}.                               \tag{26}
\]

By \(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), the positive-cell Carter
kernels apply on \(C\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with error
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}
 =C_{2/\kappa}\frac{|\mathcal J|\log|\mathcal J|}{\sqrt n}.    \tag{27}
\]
The kernel is independent of \(u\).  Replace its matched score-normal
covariance by \(\Sigma_0\); the Gaussian Hellinger calculation recorded in
\(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) contributes
\(\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)\to0\).  Applying
\(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\) first to each indicator
\(\mathbf1\{v\in A\}\), and then to the normalized loss
\(\ell_0(A)\in[0,1]\), gives the separate coverage and risk charges
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}+
 \operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C).                              \tag{28}
\]
Gaussian translation between the matched means in (24) contributes at most
the displayed finite-arrangement term \(H_C\chi_n(C)\); this follows directly
by integrating the likelihood-ratio halfspace for two equal-covariance
Gaussians and using
\(2\Phi(x/2)-1\le x/\sqrt{2\pi}\), with the harmless numerical factor
absorbed in the enumerated \(H_C\).

We also verify that the rational offset object to which the Gaussian
certificate is applied is a legal encoded experiment.  Because
\(\widehat c_n\in\mathcal K_0\), rational linear algebra gives a rational
\(z_n\in L_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) with
\(A_\Psi z_n=\widehat c_n\).  For every fixed \(u\), relative interiority and
the tangent-image condition put
\(p_0+t(z_n+Bu)\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) for all sufficiently small
positive \(t\).  Its feasible optimal branch completion has active signs
\[
 \operatorname{sgn}\{\alpha_j'(z_n+Bu)\}
 =\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat c_{n,j}+a_j'u),                  \tag{28a}
\]
with zero assigned to every incident completion.  Hence the offset semantic
cells cover \(\mathbb R^d\).  To check the separated domain, take a strict
chamber direction of the homogeneous completed fan.  Along a sufficiently
long multiple of this direction, the fixed offsets in (28a) are dominated by
the strict homogeneous slacks.  Distances from the resulting mean to every
rival closed polyhedral component therefore grow linearly: for each rival,
one rational row has gap \(t\gamma+O(1)\) with \(\gamma>0\), and
for every point \(g\) of that rival component the row inequality gives
\[
 t\gamma+O(1)\le a'(ty-g)
 \le\|a\|_{\Sigma_0}\|ty-g\|_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}.                 \tag{28b}
\]
The row is nonzero, so its \(\Sigma_0\)-norm is positive.  Taking the infimum
over \(g\) in (28b), the finitely many lower bounds eventually exceed the
fixed \(r_0\).  If there are no active cuts, there is one global semantic
label and
the separated-domain condition is immediate.  Thus the offset object has a
complete label cover, covariance \(\Sigma_0\succ0\), and a nonempty separated
domain.  Its data are rational, so
\(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\in\mathfrak E\).

Under the affirmative effective-compatible-density premise, the conditional
theorem \(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) supplies the requested replayable
finite Gaussian rule for the rational offset experiment
\(\mathfrak G_0(\widehat c_n)\), together with its outward gluing ledger.
Applying the forward Carter kernel and the score map to that rule produces
\(K_n\).  The triangle inequality, (26), and (28), followed by the chart,
tail, and rounding inequalities certified in
\(\text{def:multinomial-transfer-handle}\), gives for both semantic coverage
deficit and normalized separated-risk excess the claimed bound
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Car},n}+\operatorname{Err}_{\Sigma,n}(C)
 +\mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}
 +H_C\chi_n(C)+\mathbf1\{\chi_n(C)>\tau_n\}\\
 &\hspace{35mm}
 +\rho_{\mathrm{led},n}+\operatorname{Tail}_n(C)
 +\operatorname{Round}_n.                                     
 \end{split}                                                    \tag{29}
\]
Each term is nonnegative and is added with its certified outward sign.

For completeness, we give a schedule rather than merely asserting one.
The local expansion and
\(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) imply
\(d_n(C)+\delta_n(C)\to0\).  Use the effective enclosures of the supplied
local family, moving remainder, and rational offset to obtain rational
\(\overline\chi_n(C)\ge\chi_n(C)\) with
\(\overline\chi_n(C)\to0\), and set
\[
 \tau_n=\sqrt{\overline\chi_n(C)+n^{-2}},
 \qquad \xi_n\le n^{-1}.                                      \tag{30}
\]
An outward rational enclosure of the square root is used in the executable
record.  Then \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) after replacing it by its running
minimum, and
\(\chi_n(C)/\tau_n\to0\), so the indicator in (29) is eventually zero.
Choose Gaussian truncation, quadrature, certificate accuracy, and simplex
rounding so that each of the last three terms in (29) is at most \(n^{-1}\).
The effective premises make each such finite search terminate.  Equations
(25) and (30) imply
\(\mathfrak b_0\{\tau_n+\chi_n(C)\}\to0\); (27) tends to zero; and all
remaining terms tend to zero by construction or by
\(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\).  This proves the asserted
compact limit.  Every supremum used above is over \(C\); hence the proof makes
no honesty or risk assertion outside the chosen compact set.

\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer,
and exact windowwise repair.}
Write \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\le k\}\).  Fix \(k\).  By
\(\text{lem:compact-causal-domain}\), the relative-interior, affine-hull,
base-convergence, and compact local-expansion assumptions imply
\[
 B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n                                      \tag{31}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  By
\(\text{prop:carter-fixed-m-positive-cell}\), also
\[
 \min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\ge\kappa/2    \tag{32}
\]
eventually.  The local expansion, zero-offset centering, and
\(\text{lem:compact-moving-remainder-covariance}\) give, for each fixed
\(\ell\le k\), convergence to zero of every term in
\(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\).  Since there are only finitely many such \(\ell\),
(31)--(32) and all inequalities
\(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\le1/\ell\), \(1\le\ell\le k\), hold
simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The maximum in
\(\text{def:comparison-window-schedule}\) is then at least \(k\).  Hence
\[
 R_n^\diamond\longrightarrow\infty.                            \tag{33}
\]
Moreover, taking \(k=R_n^\diamond\) in the defining test shows that the
complete Carter, covariance, offset, boundary, and finite-arrangement error
on the selected window is bounded by a deterministic quantity
\(\rho_n\to0\).  This is the diagonal, rather than an unjustified uniform
compact-to-global, conclusion.

We next transfer finite Gaussian lower certificates.  Let
\(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  By
\(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is a finite atomic Gaussian
dual \(\mu\) of value larger than \(L\).  Its finitely many coverage and risk
support points lie in some ball \(B_k\).  Zero-offset centering and
\(\text{lem:finite-completed-arrangement-stability}\) give, for every
coverage atom in \(D_v^0\), a point of \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at
Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  Equality-face atoms retain all their
incident labels, so one point is selected for each constraint role.

For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), the same realization can be chosen in
\(H_{n,r_0}\).  Here is the needed boundary check.  When \(r_0>0\), all
zero-offset cells are cones, so distance to every rival cone is positively
homogeneous.  First replace \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), where \(t_n\downarrow0\)
is large enough that the distance margin exceeds twice the directed
Hausdorff error.  The finite-arrangement lemma then supplies a multinomial
point whose distance from every rival multinomial union is at least \(r_0\).
When \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the label at a fixed risk atom and closedness of
the finite rival union give a strictly positive atom-specific distance; the
same conclusion follows once the arrangement error is smaller than half that
distance.  Thus every finite atomic dual has, for all sufficiently large
\(n\), a lawful realization inside \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\), by (33).

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary
window-honest multinomial rule and then apply the score and covariance maps.
By \(\text{lem:bounded-semantic-transfer-by-tv}\), the change in the finite
dual objective is at most the sum of the finitely many absolute dual
coefficients times the comparison error.  If this sum is \(A_\mu<\infty\),
weak duality therefore gives
\[
 M_n^\diamond\ge L-A_\mu\rho_n                               \tag{34}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Letting \(n\to\infty\) and then
\(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^\diamond
 \ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                           \tag{35}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment gives one measurable
\(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
 \le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.                         \tag{36}
\]
No finite representation of \(K^a\) is required: Carter's Markov kernel and
total-variation contraction apply to every measurable randomized rule.  Use
the forward Carter kernel on \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\).  The exact slack identity,
the finite completed-arrangement comparison, the Gaussian covariance
replacement, and the defining inequalities for \(R_n^\diamond\) imply that
the transferred rule has window coverage at least
\(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and window separated risk at most
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.                      \tag{37}
\]
For risk points within the arrangement error of the boundary of
\(H_{r_0}\), the finite-arrangement term in the schedule includes the
following explicit restoration.  If \(r_0>0\), positive homogeneity of the
zero-offset rival cones radially sends a point at distance
\(r_0-\gamma\) to distance \(r_0\), at displacement at most
\(2R_n^\diamond\gamma/r_0\) once \(\gamma<r_0/2\).  This displacement is
charged before the schedule accepts the window.  If \(r_0=0\), approximate
the point from its incident open chambers; Gaussian-shift total variation is
continuous, and the completed equality convention retains every required
coverage label.  Finite active-set enumeration supplies these chamber
approaches, so their maximal error is one of the finite-arrangement summands
in \(\mathscr E_n(R_n^\diamond)\).  This proves (37) also at the separated-set
boundary rather than silently replacing \(r_0\) by \(r_0-o(1)\).

Apply the algebra of \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\) with all coverage
infima restricted to the window.  The repaired rule belongs to
\(\mathcal C_{n,\eta_0}^\diamond\), because
\[
 (1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0,
 \qquad q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n},                      \tag{38}
\]
and \(\eta_0+\rho_n>0\).  Since \(0\le\ell_0\le1\), (37)--(38) yield
\[
 M_n^\diamond
 \le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
 +\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.                              \tag{39}
\]
Letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combining with (35)
proves
\[
 M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow
 M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                               \tag{40}
\]

The global feasible class is a subset of the window-feasible class, and its
risk supremum is over a superset of the window risk domain.  Hence, directly
from the two minimax definitions,
\[
 M_n\ge M_n^\diamond.                                          \tag{41}
\]
Equations (40)--(41) give
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
 \ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).                            \tag{42}
\]
If the effective-compatible-density question has an affirmative answer, use
\(\text{thm:certglue-termination}\) in place of the abstract rule in (36),
with certificate accuracy tending to zero.  Its finite rule, Carter transfer,
outward errors, and repair (38) are then replayable.  This conditional
effectivity is not used to prove (33)--(42).  Finally,
\(\text{lem:escaping-boundary-kill}\) supplies arrays agreeing on every fixed
compact but having different global upper behavior.  It therefore forbids
deducing a global \(\limsup\) bound from the compact-uniform premises used
above.

\textbf{Technique: composition of exact finite-fiber identification,
rational tangent geometry, and the two transfer theorems.}
Let \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) and let \(p_0=p(P_0)\).  The
assignment, support, randomization, three consistency conditions, no-defiers,
complier-conditional selection monotonicity, and aggregate target-positivity
conditions are precisely the separate restrictions defining
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  In particular
\(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_*>0\), so every conditional quantile in the target
has a positive denominator.

By \(\text{thm:causal-label-polyhedralization}\), the displayed observed-cell
contrasts identify the selected-complier submeasures, and the finite
response-type fiber represents exactly the compatible full-law fiber.  By
\(\text{prop:lower-endpoint-attainment}\) and
\(\text{prop:upper-endpoint-attainment}\), for each fixed
\(t\in\mathcal T\) there are same-law witnesses satisfying
\[
 \begin{split}
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p_0)}(t)
 &=\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\\
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p_0)}(t)
 &=\overline\Delta(t;p_0).
 \end{split}                                                    \tag{43}
\]
For any single \(P\in\mathcal F(p_0)\), the definitions of the infimum and
supremum give, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 \underline\Delta(t;p_0)
 \le Q_{1,P}(t)-Q_{0,P}(t)
 \le\overline\Delta(t;p_0).                                   \tag{44}
\]
Taking all \(t\in\mathcal T\) and then all compatible \(P\) in (44) proves
the outer bound
\[
 \Theta_{\mathrm{ASC}}(p_0)
 \subseteq\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}
 [\underline\Delta(t;p_0),\overline\Delta(t;p_0)].             \tag{45}
\]
The witnesses in (43) may depend on \(t\) and on the chosen endpoint, so
(45) is not promoted to rectangle equality.

Under the declared relative-interior and tangent-image conditions,
\(\text{prop:tangent-fan-global-cover}\) proves
\(\bigcup_{v\in V}D_v^0=\mathbb R^d\), including every equality face in all
incident labels.  Multinomial interiority and full column rank of \(B\) give,
for every nonzero \(x\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
 x'I_0x
 =\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\frac{\{(Bx)_j\}^2}{(p_0)_j}>0.       \tag{46}
\]
Thus \(I_0\succ0\), \(\Sigma_0=I_0^{-1}\succ0\), and the covariance is
well defined.  The exact rational construction uses rational \(p_0\) and
\(B\), so \(\Sigma_0\) is rational.  Finally,
\(\text{prop:job-corps-radius-nonempty}\) proves
\(H_{r_0}\ne\varnothing\) by its violated-row distance certificate.  The
cover, covariance, and nonempty-separated-domain conditions, together with
the finite rational cells and label metric, are exactly the member conditions
of \(\mathfrak E\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak G_0\in\mathfrak E.                                 \tag{47}
\]

On every fixed compact,
\(\text{thm:fixed-stratum-transfer}\) applies Carter's bounded-ratio kernels
only to the positive multinomial cells and separately charges label geometry
and covariance replacement.  When \(c_n\to c\in\mathcal K_0\),

to give the stated compact semantic transfer; it makes no assertion outside

\[
 M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).     \tag{48}
\]
The first limit restricts both coverage and risk to one certified expanding
